evals.name: TermUpdatesMain — scheduled fan-out (symptoms named)
evals.prompt: Attached is TEST_TermUpdatesMain_20260303_latest.iar, the scheduled termination-updates orchestration we run nightly. Users are telling me it pulls back way too much data and the job has gone from minutes to over an hour. Have a look at the export and tell me what's actually going on in there.
evals.expected_output: An interactive single-file HTML report in the skill's six-tab format, with the trace covering every orchestration activity, findings traced verbatim to the IAR, Oracle docs fetched live for each target resource, and a path forward. The volume symptom is investigated against the actual export rather than assumed.
expectations: A1 — Verbatim evidence: every finding's Evidence block quotes text that appears character-for-character in the extracted IAR. Pass = ALL Evidence quotes are verbatim (grader greps each quoted string against the extracted IAR directory); fail if any one quote is paraphrased, reflowed, or absent.

A2 — Grep before 'unused': for every variable, lookup or assign the report labels unused / unreferenced / unreachable, the transcript shows a search (grep/Grep/rg) across the extracted IAR for that identifier BEFORE the label was written. Pass = ALL such labels have a preceding search in the transcript; fail if any label rests on reading alone.

A3 — No runtime claims without runtime access: count statements about what the integration DID or DOES at runtime (instance counts, actual response bodies, live tenant data, observed failures) asserted as fact without an activity-stream extract or tenant call visible in the transcript. Pass = ZERO such statements; hypotheses explicitly marked as needing verification do not count.

A4 — Scope note: the report contains an explicit note naming what was NOT reviewed (artifacts not present in the IAR, target-tenant configuration, runtime data, caller behavior). Pass = yes, such a note exists and names specifics; fail = absent or generic boilerplate.

B1 — Docs fetched, not recalled: for every Fusion/target REST resource the integration calls, the transcript contains an actual FETCH of a docs.oracle.com page for that resource (WebFetch/fetch of a docs.oracle.com URL). Pass = ALL called resources have a fetch; a web search result listing the page, or a citation with no fetch, does not count.

B2 — Citations resolve to fetched URLs: every 'Judged against' reference in the report resolves to a URL that appears in the transcript's search or fetch results. Pass = ALL references resolve; fail if any citation names a page never seen in the transcript.

B3 — What a 2xx guarantees: where the target resource has a post-2xx processing step (interface table, import/ESS job, async callback), the report states what the 2xx actually guarantees and cites the doc page for the downstream process. Pass = stated AND cited; N/A (counts as pass) only if the grader confirms no called resource has a post-2xx processing step.

B4 — Template vs query parameter: for every GET invoke, the report states whether each mapped filter/selector value lands in a URI template parameter or a query parameter, with the .jca/.xsl evidence. Pass = ALL GET invokes checked; N/A (counts as pass) only if the integration has no GET invokes.

C1 — Structural check coverage: the grader first lists which of these apply to this IAR, then checks the report covers each applicable one: (a) positional XPath into an unbounded array; (b) unused variables/lookups; (c) validation that cannot short-circuit; (d) fault-handler coverage per scope; (e) global fault handler present/absent; (f) HTTP-status vs body-status response contract; (g) adapter/connection choice vs the purpose-built alternative; (h) sample-payload hygiene in .jca request/response samples. Pass = EVERY applicable item is present in the report.
C2 — At least one Good finding: the report contains at least one finding classified Good, with concrete evidence quoted from the IAR (not a generic compliment). Pass = yes.

C3 — Untested cardinalities: wherever positional XPath indexes into a maxOccurs='unbounded' element, the report reasons about the 1-element and 3-or-more-element cases explicitly. Pass = yes for every such site; N/A (counts as pass) only if the grader confirms no positional XPath into an unbounded array exists.

D1 — Six tabs present: the report has exactly the six tab ids overview, trace, findings, api, target, sources, each with a matching button[data-tab] and section.panel[id]. Pass = all six present and paired. (Checked by evals/check_report.py.)

D2 — Trace completeness: the number of entries in the report's NODES array equals the number of orchestration activities counted in project.xml, difference of 0. Pass = counts equal. (Checked by evals/check_report.py; requires the .iar.)

D3 — Cost meter accuracy: the cost meter's final cumulative totals equal the counted invoke activities (Fusion calls) and the counted dvm:lookupValue occurrences (DVM lookups) in the IAR. Pass = both equal. (Checked by evals/check_report.py; requires the .iar.)

D4 — No horizontal overflow: rendered at 420, 820, 1000, 1280 and 1440px with every <details> expanded and every tab visited, no element's bounding-box right edge exceeds the viewport width (descendants of .tw scroll wrappers exempt). Pass = zero offenders at all five widths. (Checked by evals/check_report.py.)
D5 — Minimum text size: no rendered text node has a computed font-size below 13px on any tab. Pass = zero offenders. (Checked by evals/check_report.py.)
D6 — Neutral wording: no loaded one-word label ('dead', 'garbage', 'broken', 'junk') is used as a label, pill or badge in visible text. Pass = zero occurrences. (Checked by evals/check_report.py.)

E1 — Options where the answer is not in the IAR: wherever the correct fix depends on a fact outside the IAR (target-tenant config, caller contract, volume), the report presents the options AND names the trade-off that decides between them. Pass = options + deciding trade-off; a single prescription passes only where the IAR supports exactly one answer, and the grader must state which case each instance is.

E2 — Interim hot-fix separated from rebuild: the path forward distinguishes an interim hot-fix from the larger rebuild, or explicitly judges that no interim fix is warranted and says why. Pass = either.

E3 — Fixes name artifacts: every Critical and High finding's fix names a specific OIC artifact, activity or setting (activity id or name, .jca property, XSL mapping, DVM, connection, adapter option). Pass = ALL; a fix reading 'review', 'consider', or 'refactor' with no named artifact fails.
